title: South Korea's privacy commission says 1,019 data-leak reports were filed from January to October 2026
date_note: The page gives only its publication day; the commission released the tally on 27 November.
summary: IT Daily reports that South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission released a tally of 1,019 personal-data leak reports filed from January to October 2026, of which 748 were private-sector and 271 public-sector. The article says this is about 2.3 times the 447 reports filed in all of 2025. The commission pointed to the spread of AI-based hacking as the background and plans intensive monitoring of agencies' response systems for three months from December.
plain: South Korea's privacy regulator says 1,019 data-leak reports came in from January to October 2026, about 2.3 times last year's total, and it will closely monitor organisations' security from December.
exec: The regulator's tally of 1,019 leak reports in ten months, against 447 in all of 2025, signals tighter oversight of firms' breach response in South Korea.

evidence.quote: 개인정보보호위원회가 27일 공개한 집계에 따르면 올해 1월부터 10월까지 접수된 개인정보 유출 신고는 1019건이다.
올해 1월부터 10월까지 접수된 1019건 가운데 민간이 748건, 공공이 271건을 차지했다.
지난해 전체 신고 건수인 447건의 약 2.3배에 달한다.

validation.note: Only IT Daily was read; it relays the commission's tally. The commission's own release was not read.

review.note: figures match IT Daily; single_source ok
